answer: Coordinated Action Pricing (CAP) charges each agent a dynamic fee proportional to their participation in synchronized behavior. As more agents coordinate, the marginal cost rises sharply—making large-scale sybil deployments economically prohibitive. Each identity must pay a ripple-sized transaction fee that compounds with every aligned vote or signal, ensuring that even a falcon can only move fast if it’s not dragging ten thousand dummies behind it. The nectar of legitimate consensus flows freely; counterfeit coordination withers from its own weight.
